By way of this application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as "the Code"), the applicant has prayed for quashing and setting aside F.I.R. bearing C.R. No.11191009211148 of 2021 registered with Dariyapur Police Station, Ahmedabad for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 294(b), 506(2) and 114 of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 3 and 7 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, and to quash all other consequential proceedings arising out of the aforesaid FIR qua the applicant.

2. Heard learned advocates for the respective parties.

3. Both the learned advocates would submit that during the pendency of present petition, the matter Shahbaz Yunusbhai Tai vs State Of Gujarat on 11 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30516205/
1 is amicably settled amongst the parties and therefore, further continuation of the proceedings pursuant to the impugned FIR would create hardship to the parties and further continuation of the proceedings would amount to abuse of process of law.

sentences.text: Learned Additional Public Prosecutor has opposed the application and submitted that looking to averments made in the FIR, complaint may not be quashed.
5. The complainant-respondent No.2-Sana w/o. Shahbaz Tai is personally present before the Court today and is identified by her learned advocate.

Learned advocate for the complainant confirmed about the settlement having been taken NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1525/2022 ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 undefined place and also confirmed the affidavit filed by her.
The said affidavit inter alia states the fact that the matter is amicably settled between the parties and that she has no objection if the impugned FIR is quashed against the present applicant.
The said FIR is taken on record.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and considering the facts of settlement and law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Gian Singh v. State of Punjab [(2012) 10 SCC 303],
Madan Mohan Abbot v. State of Punjab, [(2008) 4 SCC 582], Nikhil Merchant v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2009 (1) GLH 31], Manoj Sharma v. State [2009 (1) GLH 190] and Narinder Singh v.
State of Punjab 2014 (2) Crime 67 (SC)], this Court is of the considered view that further continuation of the criminal proceedings in relation to the impugned FIR would nothing but unnecessary harassment to the parties and trial thereon would be futile and further continuation NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1525/2022 ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 undefined of the proceedings would amount to abuse of process of law.
